--- gd-head-tags: - >- ``{=html} open-graph: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random bipartite graph with given degrees on each side (configuration model). twitter-card: title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} | Edgecase description: >- Add a random bipartite graph with given degrees on each side (configuration model). title: >- [Graph.add_bipartite_configuration_model()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 bread-crumbs: false toc-depth: 3 description-meta: >- Add a random bipartite graph with given degrees on each side (configuration model). page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Add a random bipartite graph with given degrees on each side (configuration model). ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L13783-L13893){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-function} ```pythonsignature Graph.add_bipartite_configuration_model( aseq, bseq, seed=None, type=None, label=True, rel=None, part_attr="part", ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} ![Bipartite configuration model](../assets/graphs/add-bipartite-configuration-model.light.svg){.lightbox fig-alt="Three bipartite configuration models, the first part in an accent top row and the second in a teal bottom row, each node's degree in a pill. Three ones on each side give a perfect matching; three twos against two threes give six edges in which the stubs happened to pair into two doubled edges, drawn bowed apart; and 3, 2, 1 against 2, 2, 1, 1 gives six edges with one doubled. Every node meets its degree exactly, and no edge joins two nodes in the same row." width="100%"} Creates `len(aseq)` nodes in a first part and `len(bseq)` in a second, and gives first-part node `i` exactly `aseq[i]` edges and second-part node `j` exactly `bseq[j]`. Each node gets one stub per unit of degree, the two parts' stub lists are shuffled, and the stubs are paired off in order, so every edge joins the two parts. Because stubs are paired blindly, the same two nodes can be joined more than once: the result can have parallel edges (but never self-loops). `simplify()` collapses them, at the cost of exact degrees. The model is NetworkX's `bipartite.configuration_model()`. Each node's part is stored in the `part_attr=` node attribute (`0` for the first, `1` for the second). The first part is created first, and in a directed graph every edge points from the first part to the second. The graph is appended without touching or connecting to existing nodes, and the whole construction is recorded as a single step. Bipartite configuration models are useful for: - null models for two-mode networks (authors and papers, people and events) that keep every node's degree but randomize who is linked to whom - testing whether a bipartite network's projections or clustering are explained by its degrees alone - generating two-mode test data with prescribed, e.g. heavy-tailed, degrees ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [aseq]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degrees of the first-part nodes, as a list of non-negative integers. [bseq]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Degrees of the second-part nodes, as a list of non-negative integers. Must have the same sum as `aseq=`. [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Integer seed for the random number generator. The same `seed=` with the same other arguments always gives the same graph. If `None` (default), the graph differs on every call. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `type` attribute of every new node. If `None` (default), no `type` attribute is set. [label]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[True]{.va}]{.doc-parameter-default} : If `True` (default), each new node is labelled with its node ID as a string; a label that is already used raises `ValueError` before anything is added. If `False`, the nodes are left unlabelled. [rel]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Optional value stored in the `rel` attribute of every new edge. If `None` (default), no `rel` attribute is set. [part_attr]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Optional[str]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["part"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Name of the node attribute that records each node's part (`0` or `1`). Default is `"part"`. Pass `None` to skip storing it. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Self for method chaining. The graph is modified in place. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If a degree is negative or the two sequences have different sums. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Three first-part nodes of degree `2` and two second-part nodes of degree `3` share six edges: ::: {#f3fbc349 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph().add_bipartite_configuration_model([2, 2, 2], [3, 3], seed=1) graph.count_nodes(), graph.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (5, 6) ``` ::: ::: Every node gets exactly its degree, and the `part` column tells the two sides apart: ::: {#29e95290 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.get_node_df().select("label", "part", "degree") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: Edges only ever join the two parts, so the graph is bipartite even when stubs pair up twice: ::: {#a2e35c68 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} graph.is_bipartite(), graph.is_simple() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` (True, False) ``` ::: :::
